headline: Clinton ended the official 'combat zone' status for Vietnam and its nearby waters, which had been in place since the Vietnam War.
what_it_does: This order ended the combat zone designation for Vietnam and the waters around it. A combat zone designation mainly affects taxes, letting military members serving there exclude some or all of their pay from federal income tax. After this order, service in Vietnam no longer counted as combat zone service. The title alone gives no further details.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. military members serving in or near Vietnam
who_it_affects.how: They would no longer qualify for the special tax breaks tied to serving in a designated combat zone in that area.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed May 13, 1996; the termination is generally understood to have taken effect July 1, 1996, but the title alone does not confirm the date.
